ledger.note: 1607: Jamestown, the first English colony. 'The first British colony was Jamestown, established on May 14, 1607, near Chesapeake Bay.'
1620: Plymouth Colony. The page: 'culminating with Plymouth Colony in 1620'; the Pilgrims 'sailed to America in 1620 on the Mayflower'. The disc is the researcher's reading of 'Plymouth'.

1624: Virginia becomes a royal colony. The page lists Virginia 'established in 1607 as a proprietary colony; chartered as a royal colony in 1624' and says nothing about the settled extent: the whole of present Virginia is the researcher's bridging.

1628: Massachusetts Bay Colony. 'Massachusetts Bay Colony, established in 1628' (the page also has 'More Puritans immigrated in 1629 and established the Massachusetts Bay Colony with 400 settlers'); drawn as present Massachusetts, which absorbs Plymouth.
1629: New Hampshire. 'Province of New Hampshire, established in 1629; merged with Massachusetts Bay Colony in 1641; chartered as royal colony in 1679.'
1632: Maryland. 'In 1632, King Charles I granted the charter for the Province of Maryland to Cecil Calvert, 2nd Baron Baltimore'; the page gives no settlement year.
1636: Connecticut. 'Connecticut Colony, established in 1636; chartered as royal colony in 1662.'
1636: Rhode Island. 'Providence Plantations, established by Roger Williams in 1636'; royal charter 1663.

region.text: New Netherland: New York from Long Island up the Hudson and Mohawk valleys, the land between the Hudson and the Delaware, and the lower Delaware; without the Haudenosaunee homeland

ledger.note: 1664: the English take New Netherland. 'Colonel Richard Nicolls took New Amsterdam on August 27, 1664, and renamed it New York' (infobox: captured August 28, surrendered September 29); Fort Orange (Albany) surrendered on 24 September; the Duke of York 'was granted a proprietary colony which included New Netherland', and gave the land between the Hudson and the Delaware to Carteret and Berkeley (New Jersey). The Thirteen Colonies page dates Delaware's founding to 1664 as well; the Delaware settlements fell in October 1664 in the New Netherland dossier. The Haudenosaunee homeland is not part of the gain (Iroquois page: 'the Iroquois preserved considerable independence'; request R080).

certainty.note: Colonial charters gave 'sea to sea' or river-to-river grants with no survey; the shapes are the modern states of the charters and are approximate; the settled area was a coastal belt.
The Proclamation Line follows the Appalachian watershed and was moved by treaty in 1768; the boundary of New York with the Iroquois and of the colonies with Quebec stays approximate.

notes: Written to separate the colonies from the Cliopatria aggregates (English Colonial Empire 1609-1779, British Colonial Empire 1706-1999), which draw them with the Caribbean and Indian possessions (see the english-colonial-empire notes). Five pages opened: Thirteen Colonies, Province of New York, Province of Georgia, Royal Proclamation of 1763, Quebec Act. SIMPLIFICATION: the pages give charters and founding years, not settled areas, so each colony enters as its modern state at the year the page gives (Virginia and Plymouth as discs first); the interior was unsettled until the 1763 line cut the west. Not on the pages opened: Maine's attachment to Massachusetts (1650s), Vermont and the New Hampshire Grants, the Dominion of New England's effect (1685-1689: 'closed in 1689'), the 1739-1748 war, the French and Indian War front, 1775 outbreak of the Revolution, the 1783 treaty's lands. The Quebec Act of 1774 (assent 22 June 1774, infobox commencement 13 January 1774, 'roughly tripling its size') took the Ohio country for Quebec over the objections of New York, Pennsylvania and Virginia; the dossier does not draw those lands as colonial. Disagreements: New York capture 27 August (text) vs 28 August (infobox); surrender 24/29 September; the Treaty of Breda 1667 vs Westminster 1674 as the end of Dutch claim; Georgia royal colony 1751/1752/1755; New York a royal colony 1685 (text) vs 1689 (infobox) vs 1686 (Thirteen Colonies page). The counterpart for the 1664 gain is new-netherland (its own ledger names english-colonial-empire as the taker). Capitals: none, the colonies had no common seat (the crown governed them from London). Region names missing from the gazetteer: none new (all by modern states and discs). Needs dossiers: east-florida / west-florida (British Florida 1763-1783), province-of-quebec (1763-1791).
